english.title: Unauthorised acts with intent to impair operation of or prevent / hinder access to a computer
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) did an unauthorised act at a time when you knew that it was unauthorised either intending by doing the act or being reckless as to whether the act would

(A)_[impair the operation of a computer]_
(B)_[prevent or hinder access to a program or data held in a computer]_
(C)_[impair the operation of a program or the reliability of data held in a computer]_
(D)_[enable the operation of a computer to be impaired, access to a program or data held in a computer to be prevented or hindered, or the operation of a program or the reliability of data held in a computer to be impaired]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 3(1) and (6) of the Computer Misuse Act 1990.

english.notes:
(i) This offence was substituted by section 36 of the Police and Justice Act 2006.
(ii) Section 3(3) of the Act (as inserted by section 36(3) of the Police and Justice Act 2006) provides that this will apply if the person is reckless as to whether the act will do any of the things mentioned above.
(iii) Section 3(4) of the Act (as inserted by section 36(4) of the Police and Justice Act 2006) provides that the intention referred to in this offence or the recklessness referred to in Note (iii) above, need not relate to any particular computer, any particular program or data or a program or data of any particular kind.

other.penalty:
Either Way
Summary: 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: 10 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2002; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 3(6)(a) of the Computer Misuse Act 1990 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
